title: The Reporting-Guidelines Map — CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD and More

hook.en: Every kind of study has a recipe for how it should be reported, written by international experts. Following it makes your paper clear, complete and much more likely to be accepted. Not knowing it is like cooking without the ingredient list. Here is the map.
hook.ur: Har qism ke study ki report ka ek nuskha hota hai jo beinul-aqwami maahireen ne likha. Iska follow karna aap ke paper ko saaf, mukammal aur manzoor hone ke zyada qabil banata hai. Ise na jaanna ajzaa ki list ke baghair pakane jaisa hai. Yeh naqsha hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll match a study design to its reporting guideline (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD, SRQR, COREQ and others), find guidelines through the EQUATOR Network and use the checklist before you write and before you submit.
goal.ur: End tak aap study design ko uski reporting guideline (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD, SRQR, COREQ aur doosri) se milayenge, EQUATOR Network se guidelines dhoondhenge aur likhne se pehle aur bhejne se pehle checklist istemal karenge.

text.en: A **reporting guideline** is a checklist of what a paper must say so readers can judge and repeat the study. Each design has its own. The **EQUATOR Network** (equator-network.org) is a free library of them. Journals often ask for the checklist at submission. Using it **while planning** also improves the study itself, because you notice what you must record and measure. A reporting guideline is not a quality score; it tells you what to report, not how good the study was.
text.ur: **Reporting guideline** woh checklist hai jo batati hai paper mein kya hona chahiye taake parhne wale study ko jaanch aur dohra saken. Har design ki apni hai. **EQUATOR Network** (equator-network.org) in ki muft library hai. Journals aksar bhejte waqt checklist mangte hain. **Plan karte waqt** isay istemal karna study ko bhi behtar karta hai, kyunke aap dekhte hain kya record aur naapna hai. Reporting guideline quality score nahi; yeh batati hai kya report karna hai, study kitni achhi thi yeh nahi.

text.en: Think of **a recipe card in a restaurant kitchen**. It lists every ingredient and step so that any cook can make the same dish. A reporting guideline is the recipe card for a study: with it, another researcher can understand exactly what you did, and a reader can tell if something is missing.
text.ur: **Restaurant ke bawarchi khane mein recipe card** sochein. Yeh har ajzaa aur qadam batati hai taake koi bhi bawarchi wohi dish bana sake. Reporting guideline study ki recipe card hai: is ke saath doosra muhaqqiq theek theek samajh sakta hai aap ne kya kiya, aur parhne wala jaan sakta hai kuch kam to nahi.

question.en: You are writing up a survey of 300 physiotherapists. Which guideline is most relevant?
question.ur: Aap 300 physiotherapists ke survey ki report likh rahe hain. Kaun si guideline sab se mutaliq hai?

feedback.ur: Yeh randomised trials ke liye hai.
Yeh systematic reviews ke liye hai.

text.en: STROBE, for cross-sectional studies (and CHERRIES if it is a web survey)
text.ur: STROBE, cross-sectional studies ke liye (aur agar web survey ho to CHERRIES)

feedback.en: Yes — a survey is a cross-sectional design.

question.ur: Apne study design ki sahi reporting guideline kahan mil sakti hai?

text.ur: Sirf kisi ek journal ki website mein

feedback.ur: Journals EQUATOR ka link dete hain.

text.en: The EQUATOR Network library at equator-network.org
text.ur: equator-network.org par EQUATOR Network ki library

question.en: When is the best time to use a reporting checklist?
question.ur: Reporting checklist istemal karne ka behtareen waqt kaun sa hai?

text.en: While planning the study, and again while writing, so you capture what you need to report
text.ur: Study plan karte waqt, aur dobara likhte waqt, taake jo report karna hai woh hasil ho

feedback.en: Yes — using it early improves the study.
feedback.ur: Haan — jaldi istemal study ko behtar karta hai.

text.en: Only after the paper is accepted
text.ur: Sirf paper manzoor hone ke baad

text.en: Never, if the study is small
text.ur: Kabhi nahi, agar study chhota ho

text.en: **Treating the checklist as a box to tick at the end.** If you complete CONSORT when the paper is finished, you may find you never recorded blinding or drop-outs. Use it at the planning stage. Also, do not confuse reporting with quality: a paper can tick every box and still be a poor study. And do not paste the checklist and say "see supplement" without really addressing each item in the paper.
text.ur: **Checklist ko aakhir mein tick karne ka dibba samajhna.** Agar aap paper khatam hone par CONSORT bharein to ho sakta hai pata chale ke blinding ya drop-outs kabhi record hi nahi kiye. Planning ke marhale mein istemal karein. Reporting ko quality se na milayein: paper har dibba tick kar ke bhi kharab study ho sakta hai. Aur checklist paste kar ke "supplement dekhein" na kahein bina paper mein har item ko sach mein hal kiye.

text.en: **Make a small cheat sheet.** Print the checklist for the design you use most, such as CARE for case reports, and stick it on your desk. When you appraise a paper, use the same checklist to find gaps. Journals and ethics committees are more likely to trust a submission with the checklist attached.
text.ur: **Chhoti cheat sheet banayein.** Jis design ko aap sab se zyada istemal karte hain, jaise case reports ke liye CARE, uski checklist print kar ke apni mez par lagayein. Paper parakhte waqt kamiyan dhoondhne ke liye wohi checklist istemal karein. Journals aur ethics committees checklist ke saath bheji gayi submission par zyada bharosa karte hain.

answer.en: Because studies of the literature found that many papers left out essential details: how participants were allocated, what happened to those who dropped out, what exactly the treatment was. Without these, readers cannot judge bias or repeat the work. The EQUATOR Network was set up to collect guidelines and promote their use, and journals that require them see clearer reports.
answer.ur: Kyunke literature ke jaiza studies ne paya ke bohat se papers ne ahem tafseelat chhor di: shirkat karne walon ko kaise tay kiya gaya, jo chhor gaye un ka kya hua, ilaaj bilkul kya tha. In ke baghair parhne wale bias parakh nahi sakte ya kaam dohra nahi sakte. EQUATOR Network guidelines jama karne aur unke istemal ko farogh dene ke liye bana, aur jo journals unhein lazmi qarar dete hain wahan reports aam taur par zyada saaf hoti hain.

beats.patient: A student is writing up a randomised pilot of a home exercise programme and a separate qualitative study of participants' experiences. She wonders what to use.
beats.assessment: A randomised pilot calls for CONSORT (with its pilot extension) and TIDieR for the programme; the interviews call for COREQ.
beats.treatment: She downloads each checklist from EQUATOR, uses them during planning and again when writing, and attaches the completed lists to her submissions.
beats.reassess: Reviewers find the papers clear and complete, and ask for few changes.

text.en: **Report harms with the same care as benefits.** Most guidelines require reporting of adverse events and harms. Do not leave them out because the numbers are small or the results look negative. Readers need to see the whole picture, especially when a technique could cause serious harm.
text.ur: **Nuqsan ki report faide jitni ehtiyat se karein.** Zyada tar guidelines adverse events aur nuqsan ki report lazmi karti hain. Unhein is liye na chhorein ke numbers chhote hain ya nateeje manfi lagte hain. Parhne walon ko poori tasveer dekhni chahiye, khaaskar jab technique seriyas nuqsan kar sake.

text.en: The EQUATOR Network was established to improve the reliability and value of the published health research literature by promoting transparent and accurate reporting, and maintains a library of reporting guidelines. The STROBE statement lists 22 items that should be addressed in reports of cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies, aimed at improving the quality of reporting of observational studies.
text.ur: EQUATOR Network is liye qaim hui ke shaya shuda sehat research ki bharosemandi aur qeemat shaffaf aur durust report ko farogh de kar behtar ho, aur reporting guidelines ki library rakhti hai. STROBE statement 22 items batata hai jin ka cohort, case-control aur cross-sectional studies ki reports mein zikr hona chahiye, jis ka maqsad observational studies ki report ki quality behtar karna hai.

text.en: **Match, Find, Use early.** Match the design to its guideline, find it on EQUATOR, and use it from the planning stage.
text.ur: **Milayein, Dhoondhein, Jaldi istemal.** Design ko uski guideline se milayein, EQUATOR par dhoondhein, aur planning se istemal karein.

summary.en: Each study design has its own reporting guideline: CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD, COREQ, SQUIRE and more.
summary.ur: Har study design ki apni reporting guideline hai: CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD, COREQ, SQUIRE aur mazeed.

summary.en: Find them for free through the EQUATOR Network and use them while planning, not only at the end.
summary.ur: Unhein EQUATOR Network se muft dhoondhein aur sirf aakhir mein nahi, planning mein istemal karein.

summary.en: A guideline tells you what to report, not how good the study was; report harms as carefully as benefits.
summary.ur: Guideline batati hai kya report karna hai, study kitni achhi thi yeh nahi; nuqsan ki report faide jitni ehtiyat se karein.
